title: The unit kernel at a point on the closed image
statement: Let i:Z -> Y be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], F an O_Y-module, and z a point of Z. For the adjunction chosen by nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction [def-pc-module-pullback], let eta_F:F -> i_*i^*F be its unit. Let S be the module stalk functor at i(z) [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Then ker(S(eta_F)) = ker(i.stalkMap z) times the whole module F_i(z), as submodules of F_i(z). This concerns only the local ring kernel, not the scheme ideal sheaf or its multiplication map.

proof.text: For a surjective ring map f:R -> T and R-module M, tensor the exact pair ker(f) -> R -> T with M using Mathlib rTensor_exact. Precompose with the inverse left unitor R tensor M -> M. Mathlib Submodule.map_range_rTensor_subtype_lid computes the transported range as ker(f) times M. Thus ker(m -> 1 tensor m) = ker(f) times M.

For the canonical adjunction, the closed-pushforward stalk map is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Compose it with the tensor pullback stalk comparison. The two germ formulas show on every representative that this additive equivalence sends the unit to m -> 1 tensor m. Its injectivity preserves the kernel. Apply the first step to i.stalkMap z, which is surjective by the closed-immersion hypothesis.

Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app expresses the unit of the chosen adjunction as the canonical unit followed by the pushforward of an isomorphism. Applying S preserves that isomorphism; its injectivity leaves the kernel unchanged.

from.place: Step 7, essential-surjectivity: the closed-immersion quotient dictionary. This isolates the unit kernel at a point on the closed image.

lean.statement:
theorem closedImmersion_unit_stalk_kernel_on_image {Y Z : Scheme.{w}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (F : Y.Modules) (z : Z) :
    let adj := Classical.choice (nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)
    let S := RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace (i.base z)
    LinearMap.ker (S.map (adj.unit.app F)).hom =
      RingHom.ker (i.stalkMap z).hom •
        (⊤ : Submodule (Y.presheaf.stalk (i.base z)) (S.obj F))
